video.title: Portland Trail Blazers Fantasy Basketball Preview - Return Of Damian Lillard

summary: Josh Lloyd previews the Portland Trail Blazers for fantasy. The main question is who handles the ball now that Damian Lillard is back, Ja Morant has arrived, and Scoot Henderson is healthy alongside Deni Avdija and Jrue Holiday. He thinks Avdija's usage and assists have to drop, so he moves him to round three or four. Lillard is his best target: he says Lillard is a top 50 player who could reach top 35, and a pick in the 50s is fine. Donovan Clingan is his biggest fade. He calls Clingan a two-category player (rebounds and blocks) who belongs in the 60s or 70s, not the 30s or 40s. Scoot Henderson is his late-round swing, Robert Williams is a stash for formats that allow it, and he would not draft Toumani Camara in 12-team leagues.

rules.text: Do not draft strictly by rank order. Tiny projection differences, like a free throw percentage moving from 83.4 to 82.6, can shift a player from 30th to 39th, and that difference does not matter.
rules.quote: I've got this guy at 83.4 from the line, and what if he shoots 82.6?

rules.text: Look at the next 12 to 15 names on your projection list and pick for team fit and category needs, even if that means taking a player before where you projected him.
rules.quote: So I look at the first 12 names on my projection list, sometimes down to 15.

rules.text: Z-score rankings can overrate players who are elite in only one or two categories. Be wary of two-category bigs early in drafts.
rules.quote: because there are flaws in the way that a standard score, a Zed score shows value.

rules.text: Big men like Walker Kessler or Rudy Gobert should give a strong FG% to justify a high pick.
rules.quote: when you have this archetype, Walker Kesler, Rudy Gobert, you want field goals 52%.

rules.text: Steals are a fickle category year to year.
rules.quote: they just didn't come because they're a fickle c category.

rules.text: Threes are abundant in the NBA, so a player's three-point production should not be overvalued.
rules.quote: Tammani Kamar is hitting 2.7 a game. Threes are abundant in the NBA.

rules.text: Being named a starter matters for fantasy because it opens up more minutes.
rules.quote: when you start there's just more opportunities to play more minutes and that's important for us.

rules.text: Some players scale their usage up or down a lot with their role. Big numbers from a large role on a thin roster may not carry over when more ball handlers arrive.
rules.quote: he is a guy that can go from 24 to 16 usage.

rules.text: A backup big who would start if the starter got hurt is worth stashing in formats that allow it.
rules.quote: in stashable formats, Rob Williams, cuz if Klingan does get hurt and Rob is all right

rules.text: A team with a few more back-to-backs than the minimum barely changes the outlook for a player who will rest on back-to-backs.
rules.quote: two extra backto-backs over the course of 23 weeks or however long your season goes.

rules.text: A meniscus repair means a longer recovery than a meniscus trim.
rules.quote: repair, not the trim. So, that makes it a longer recovery.

player_notes.text: Was the team's best player last season, but he expects Avdija to take a hit this season.
player_notes.quote: Denny Abdia who I think is almost certainly taking a hit this season to a degree.

player_notes.text: Says he cannot keep his assist rate and usage with Morant and Lillard on the roster.
player_notes.quote: I think it's impossible to maintain the same assist rate and the same usage.

player_notes.text: Projected around 46. Right spot is round three, more likely round four. He would not take him in round two. He calls ESPN's rank of 60 silly.
player_notes.quote: But round three, but more likely round four is the right spot.

player_notes.text: Profile is assists plus above average rebounds from a forward. Free throws are not his selling point.
player_notes.quote: I'm not caring about his free throws, but those assists are

player_notes.text: His best target on the team. Says Lillard is a top 50 player who could be top 35, and he will happily take him in the 50s.
player_notes.quote: I think he's a top 50 player this season. I think he could be a top 35 player.

player_notes.text: Expects him to sit back-to-backs. Rejects the idea that he will be a 25-minute bench player.
player_notes.quote: I think he will sit back to backs. No question about that.

player_notes.text: Preseason looks encouraging: 14 points in 21 minutes with 24 usage and two steals.

player_notes.text: A two-category player: elite rebounds and good blocks, low points, few assists and steals, and a FG% that is weak for a center.
player_notes.quote: cuz he can't catch the ball and he can't finish. He's like a two category player.

player_notes.text: His biggest fade. He would take Clingan in the 60s or 70s, not at his current price in the 30s or 40s.
player_notes.quote: this is a pick in the 60s or 70s, not in the 30s or 40s.

player_notes.text: Started hitting threes at 34% last season. He could hit more threes and get close to two blocks, but he is not projected for 30 minutes.
player_notes.quote: He did start to hit threes and he did it at 34% and that got better

player_notes.text: Should not be drafted in 12-team formats. His usage gets even smaller with Scoot, Dame and Ja around. Minutes are safe.

player_notes.text: His guess for the fifth starter, with low confidence. Late-round swing, but not a must-draft. He could get pulled early for Jrue or Morant.
player_notes.quote: considering in those late rounds if he does get the starting job. The problem's still going to be

player_notes.quote: He's never had a season at 50% over two, which is a big big problem.

player_notes.text: Likely a bench player playing 27 to 28 minutes. Reasonable in the 80s in points leagues, but he would not take him in the top 90 in category leagues.
player_notes.quote: I don't think I would do it in the top 90 though for a category league

player_notes.quote: Do I feel good about 90% from the line absolutely not do I think he's still a bad three-point shooter yes

player_notes.text: A very scalable player whose usage can swing from 24 to 16 depending on his role.
player_notes.quote: Drew is an unbelievably scalable player.

player_notes.quote: If you're in a 14 team league, he's a really good draft pick in that 130 to 140 range.

player_notes.quote: He got you 1.5 blocks on a ridiculous 71%. His free throws are also very weird.

player_notes.text: Not draftable in 12-team leagues as a backup. He is a stash, with top 60ish upside if Clingan gets hurt and Williams stays healthy.
player_notes.quote: that is a top 60ish upside player. It's that's why it's only Stashy

player_notes.quote: So, maybe maybe in March we see a return.

team_notes.text: Projected starters: Scoot Henderson, Damian Lillard, Toumani Camara, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan. Only the fifth spot is uncertain.
team_notes.quote: Lock in Dame, Kamar, Aia, and Klingan. They're starting.

team_notes.text: Morant is likely a bench player. Jrue Holiday or Scoot Henderson starts most nights. A first-time coach may mix up the lineup.
team_notes.quote: I actually think that it's firming more that Morant is going to be a a bench player

team_notes.text: The rotation is thin after the eighth man, especially at forward.
team_notes.quote: after the eighth guy in the rotation, it's pretty rough.

team_notes.text: Schedule: 10 games if your season ends March 28 (weak). 11 games if it ends April 4. The team has 15 back-to-backs.
team_notes.quote: If you end April 4th, Yahoo's default 434, a little bit better, 11 games, and they got 15 back to back.
